messages:
Sophie: Heads up — spotted a surprising mypy/pyright disagreement on the Python SDK pagination helpers. My autogenerated client returns an async generator typed as AsyncIterator[Optional[ItemModel]] but in practice the generator yields ItemModel only. mypy is fine but pyright reports a bunch of Optional handling required by callers.

Alex: ugh, that sounds like a stub vs runtime mismatch. can you drop a tiny repro?

Sophie: repro below — minimal client usage: 
```py
async for it in client.list_items(project_id="x"):
    # pyright flags `it` as possibly None here, suggests Optional[ItemModel]
    print(it.id)
```
The autogen produced: AsyncIterator[Optional[ItemModel]] because the model factory uses `maybe_none` helper when fields are all optional. But the pagination wrapper unwraps pages and never yields None.

Jamal: I ran into this earlier with streaming responses. Pyright's stricter nullability rules mean Optional in the signature triggers a lot of defensive checks for callers. We should prefer the concrete yield type if generator never yields None.

Maya: what's the root cause in the codegen? Is it the model being Optional because of JSON schema?

Sophie: yup, exactly. The autogen model has a bunch of Optional[...] fields, so the autogen typing for the factory is Optional[ItemModel] in some code paths. The pagination wrapper didn't refine the type.

Alex: Options: 1) change the generator stub to AsyncIterator[ItemModel] (preferred UX), 2) keep current types but add pyright/mypy suppression comments, or 3) add an explicit TypedAlias for PageItem = ItemModel to make intent clear. 1 seems best but might be a breaking change for anyone relying on Optional semantics.

Jamal: We should audit whether any generator actually yields None. If none do, we can safely tighten. Add a runtime assertion in the pagination util to guarantee non-None yields so behavior is explicit. That helps both runtime correctness and typing.

Sophie: I mocked a quick check across a few generated clients — none yield None. I'll open a tiny PR to change the return annotation in the pagination wrapper and add a unit test asserting no None yields. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 (WIP).

Alex: please also add a short migration note in the changelog — call it a typing refinement so folks searching for Optional are aware.

Maya: for pyright it's also worth adding a test in devex that runs pyright against the stubs to catch regressions (we only run mypy today). Could be a GH Action.

Sophie: good call — I'll toss a separate small action that runs pyright on the stubs directory.

ci-bot: build passed for linux/py38, failing on pyright check (expected) — see details: ci.redwood.ai/432/pyright

Jamal: one more thing — consider emitting a narrow stub for `list_items` overloads: 
```py
@overload
def list_items(..., *, raw_pages: Literal[False]) -> AsyncIterator[ItemModel]: ...
@overload
def list_items(..., *, raw_pages: Literal[True]) -> AsyncIterator[PageType]: ...
```
That gives precise types depending on flags and keeps backwards compat for `raw_pages` callers.

Sophie: love that. I'll add overloads in the PR.

Alex: assign the PR to Jamal for the runtime assertion review, Sophie for types + tests, and I'll write the changelog blurb.

Sophie: assigned. thanks y'all. :thumbsup:

Maya: quick follow-up — can we also document the expected invariants in the SDK dev guide (autogen -> pagination contract)? Would've saved me 20 minutes earlier.

Sophie: will add a short section in devex docs under autogen notes.

ci-bot: pr #432 updated by Sophie (force-pushed).

Alex: once green let's ship to our canary and watch type complaints in Sentry (if any) for the next 48h.

Jamal: noted — I'll add a quick eval that runs a few sampleapps with pyright enabled to catch user-facing warnings.

Sophie: thanks everyone — closing this thread after the merge.
